newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf plans asset sale to pay down debt.
newsitem.headline: Gulf plans asset sale to pay down debt.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd plans to sell a major northern Alberta oil and gas property it acquired last year to fund the paydown of Stampeder Exploration Ltd's debt, Gulf Chief Executive J.P. Bryan said on Monday.
Bryan said he believed the property, which pumps out about 12,500 barrels of oil equivalent a day, could fetch between C$350 million and C$400 million.
The sale and Gulf's planned public offering of its Indonesia assets provide enough cash to pay down debt to a level where Gulf's credit could be investment grade, he said.
Stampeder, target of a C$1 billion friendly takeover by Gulf, has long-term debt of about C$300 million.
"When we do the Asamera transaction, we anticipate taking another C$400-500 million off our Canadian debt and bringing it down below C$2 billion," Bryan said.

"So we think that based on cash flow multiples, debt-to-equity will be in a very comfortable range and remove once and for all the conversation about our balance sheet. We should definitely be inverstment grade at that point in time."
Gulf made a major purchase last year from Pennzoil Co last year to beef up its land position at Zama/Virgo.
It plans to market the offering of the Gulf Indonesia Resources Ltd (formerly Asamera) through September.
Bryan said the Gulf share issue tied to the Stampeder purchase would increase its number of shares outstanding by about 25 percent.
But he said he expected the effects of the dilution would be reduced by several opportunities within Stampeder's asset base.

Besides heavy oil, which would be folded into Gulf's heavy oil sands assets to form a new public company that could acquire more heavy oil assets worldwide, Stampeder's oil and gas marketing assets would also fit nicely with Gulf's own, he said.
He also said Gulf could blend Stampeder's light oil production to its heavy oil to reduce the effects of current wide light-heavy spreads.
Bryan said Gulf was paying between C$5 and C$5.50 per barrel of oil equivalent for its Stampeder's oil and gas reserves.
Those totalled 98 million barrels of proven reserves and 143 million barrels of proven and probable reserves at the end of 1996.
He also said the price represented just under five times Stampeder's expected 1998 cash flow.

Stampeder's production in the first quarter was about 32,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day, indluding 25,000 barrels of oil and liquids and 75 million cubic feet of gas a day. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
